sections.overview: The lesser yellowlegs breeds in boreal North America and winters from the southern United States to South America.
sections.identification: Its long bright-yellow legs and slender, straight bill distinguish it from many other waders; it is smaller and shorter-billed than the greater yellowlegs.
sections.habitat: It nests in open boreal forest near marshes and bogs, then uses a wide range of freshwater and coastal wetlands during migration and winter.
sections.diet: It takes aquatic and terrestrial insects, worms, small crustaceans and some small fish while foraging in shallow water and along wetland shores.
sections.behavior: It migrates between North American breeding grounds and wintering areas across Central and South America and the Caribbean.
sections.reproduction: Both parents care for the chicks, but the female usually leaves the breeding grounds before they can fly.
sections.ecology: It is a Tringa close relative of the spotted redshank; see that profile for comparison.
sections.conservation: A Chilean biodiversity assessment reports evidence of declines and identifies wetland loss, pollution, hunting and climate change as concerns; those regional findings should not be read as a current global category.
